cards.text: Friend, the trick questions are OVER. After Jesus' last answer, nobody dares ask Him anything else (Luke 20:40). So now Jesus asks a question of His own, about the Christ, the Messiah (John 1:41).

cards.question: Jesus asks how it can be said that the Christ is the son of which king?

cards.text: Then Jesus quotes the book of Psalms, where David himself tells of the Lord speaking to someone. Friend, listen CLOSE to what David calls that someone.

cards.question: In David's psalm, the Lord speaks to someone. Where does the Lord tell Him to sit?

answers.text: At the head of the table

cards.question: In David's psalm, the one at the Lord's right hand sits there until something happens to His enemies. What is it?

answers.text: They become a footstool for His feet
They run off to a far country

cards.question: Jesus points out that in this psalm, David calls the Christ ___.

cards.text: So Jesus asks, 'So how can He be David's son?' I'm the Papa, friend, and if I ever bowed to little Chip and called him 'Lord,' Mags would announce it to the WHOLE kitchen.
Then, with all the people listening, Jesus turns to His disciples and says, 'Beware of the scribes.' First up: their wardrobe.

cards.question: What does Jesus say the scribes like to walk around in?
Jesus says the scribes love to take the lowest seats at banquets.

cards.text: Not even close: they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and the only greeting I ever got was dust landing on my mustache.

cards.question: Jesus says the scribes defraud widows of their houses, and for a show they make lengthy ___.
Jesus says these scribes will receive a greater reward.

cards.text: Then Jesus looks up and sees the rich putting their gifts into the treasury. Friend, I was bought for one quarter, so watching the rich give makes me feel like pocket change.
And then He sees a poor widow. Jesus just warned about widows losing their houses, friend, so keep your eyes on this one.

cards.question: The poor widow puts two small ___ coins into the treasury.
After watching the gifts go in, Jesus says the poor widow has put in more than all the others.
Two small coins beat all those gifts from the rich? Why does Jesus say the poor widow put in more?

answers.text: She put in all she had to live on
Her two coins were old and very rare
She gave in secret and told no one

cards.question: Jesus says the others gave out of their ___, but she gave out of her ___.

findings.problem: "After Jesus' last answer, nobody dares ask Him anything else" stretches Luke 20:40. That verse says only that "they" (the scribes and Sadducees questioning Him) did not dare to question Him any further.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "So now Jesus asks a question of His own" makes Jesus' question in 20:41 a result of nobody else asking (20:40). The text only says "Then Jesus declared" and leaves open how the two connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the next words of the quoted psalm line ("Sit at My right hand"). It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not the movement or meaning of Jesus' argument.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess how the quoted psalm line ends ("a footstool for Your feet"). This is guessing the wording of a line, like the Psalm 23 anointing-oil bad example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The right answer "Lord" is capitalized and the wrong answers "son" and "servant" are lowercase, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question, but the wrong answer "Plain work clothes" is not a real detail from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: "Jesus just warned about widows losing their houses, friend, so keep your eyes on this one" ties the poor widow to the scribes' defrauding of widows. The text never makes that connection and leaves it open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
